decisions.question: Where does the saved text of issue #1 go when the history moves to docs/history/?
decisions.options: (1) stay-in-docs: the file keeps its path docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md, and the 57 other files of its folder move. Each text in force is then in docs/, and nothing in docs/history/ is in force. docs/ has 5 files with 20,625 words after step 9. 16 lines in 5 moved files get a new path (6 of them in the frozen audit record), and the file needs one status line. (2) move-with-folder: the file moves with its folder, and contract line 7 keeps the link and the words "remains binding". 4 files with 10,385 words stay in docs/, which is the count of D-CODE-04. 2 lines change beyond the move (contract line 48 and .gitattributes:5). docs/history/ then holds one file in force and needs a README that names it. (3) end-binding: the file moves, and contract line 7 says that it is no longer in force; each rule that must stay goes into the contract first. Effort L, with a review of each rule by the maintainer. It opens a part of D-CODE-04 again (the option "A short contract with a word limit", not selected). The words in force are the same in options 1 and 2.
decisions.recommended: move-with-folder. It is the count that the answer to D-CODE-04 already has, it is the smallest change, and it keeps the frozen audit folder complete. The rule that keeps the file in force is contract line 7, which stays in docs/. Wrong if the maintainer wants the rule "nothing in docs/history/ is in force" (then option 1), or if the saved issue #1 text must no longer be in force (then option 3).

decisions.question: What does the service write to D1 for a GitHub webhook that starts no work?
decisions.options: (1) keep-receipts: a receipt for each webhook as today, 4 rows and 215 bytes each with no end; 264 rows for the example commit (33 check runs, 66 webhooks by assumption, 1 with work); D1 keeps a row for each delivery. (2) one-statement: one new function says if a webhook can start work; a webhook with no work gets one INSERT that is already processed: 2 rows in place of 4 (measured, local D1), 134 rows for the example; the table grows as today. (3) no-receipt: the same function; a webhook with no work gets a log line and the 202, and no row: 4 rows for the example. The recovery settles an answered delivery without a receipt (apps/web/src/operations/github-deliveries.ts:236-239). D1 then has no list of these deliveries; GitHub lists a delivery for 3 days and Cloudflare keeps a Worker log for 7 days. One rare case writes more: a webhook with no work that GitHub lists as failed gets a redelivery request. No option deletes an existing row, so D-DATA-04 stays as answered.
decisions.recommended: no-receipt. It writes nothing for the webhooks that start no work (65 of 66 in the example), and no statement of the code lists or counts their rows. Receipts are the largest group of repeated D1 writes in the estimate of the audit. Wrong if the maintainer wants a D1 row for each delivery as an audit record (then option 2), or wants no function that sorts events before the receipt (then option 1). Money is small in each option: 0.61 USD each month at most in the estimate.
